The Sphinx Tantalizing
the Bourgeois Mind
SPHINY
On the dawn of March 18, Paris arose to the thunder-burst
of 'Vive la Commune!' What is the Commune, that sphinx
so tantalizing to the bourgeois mind? - Karl Marx
THE DIALECTICAL
RUPTURE
The Commune was not a mere
change of administration. It was
the positive form of a "social
republic" aimed at superseding
class rule itself. It was the
political form at last discovered
to work out the economic
emancipation of labor.

The Conflict
Paris could not be defended against Prussia
without arming its working class. But Paris
armed was the revolution armed.
The Betrayal
For the bourgeois government, a victory of the French
workers over Prussia was more terrifying than a Prussian

On January 28, 1871, Paris was starved into surrender.
The French army handed over its weapons, but the armed
workers--the National Guard--refused. They kept their cannons.

The Event
March 18, 1871. Thiers sends troops
on a nocturnal expedition to steal the
artillery of the National Guard, claiming
they are state property.
The Fact
The cannons were paid for by public
subscription by the workers
themselves.
The Reversal
The regular soldiers refuse to fire on
unarmed crowds, fraternize with the
people, and turn on their own
commanders. Thiers' army evaporates.
Paris is in the hands of the workers.

The working class cannot simply lay hold of the ready-made
state machinery, and wield it for its own purposes.
The Ready-Made State
Standing

The Explanation: The modern bourgeois state is an engine of class despotism. Its hierarchical
division of labor exists specifically to suppress the producing masses. It cannot be reformed; its physical
and spiritual forces of repression must be entirely amputated.

The Blueprint of the Commune State
The Communal
Constitution
The Wards
The Standing Army
Abolished. Replaced by the armed
people (National Guard).
The Police
Stripped of political attributes.
Turned into responsible, revocable
agents of the Commune.
The Legislature
Not a talking shop, but a working
body-executive and legislative at
the same time.
The Representation
Built on universal suffrage. All
delegates bound by mandat
impératif (formal instructions)
and subject to immediate recall.

The Dashboard of Decrees
Political
Dismantling
Abolished conscription.
Capped all administrative
salaries at 6,000 francs.
Judicial functionaries made
elective and revocable.
Economic
Emancipation
Abolished night work for bakers.
Closed municipal pawnshops (a
private exploitation of labor).
Handed closed factories over to
cooperative societies of workmen.
Social & Secular
Reforms
Separated Church and State.
Excluded religious dogmas and
symbols from schools.
Made education accessible and
gratuitous to all.

The Flag of the World Republic
The Action
On May 16, the Commune ordered the demolition
of the Vendôme Column-a colossal monument
cast from captured guns by Napoleon,
representing martial glory and chauvinism.
The Meaning
The Commune explicitly rejected nationalism.
While the French bourgeoisie hunted Germans,
the Commune made a German working man
its Minister of Labor. It placed heroic sons of
Poland at the head of the defense of Paris.
The Legacy
The Commune annexed to France the working
people all over the world.

The Threat to Versailles
The ruling class knew that three months
of free communication between
Communal Paris and the French
provinces would spark a general uprising
of the peasants.
The Promise to the Peasant
The Commune declared the originators of
the war would pay for it. It promised to
replace the tax-gatherer, the notary, and
the gendarme with cheap government
and salaried communal agents.
The Reality
The Commune was the true
representative of all the healthy
elements of French society.

The Dual Encirclement
Bismarck's
Prussian Army
Paris
Thiers' Versailles Army
The Trap
Paris was geographically and politically strangled. To the
north and east, the victorious Prussian army maintained a
strict blockade. To the west and south, the treacherous French
army of Versailles assembled to crush their own capital.
The Conspiracy
Thiers begged Bismarck to release French prisoners of
war from Sedan and Metz specifically to build an army
large enough to slaughter the Parisian workers.

The Complicity of Empires
The Class War
The Franco-Prussian war proved to be a mere
governmental humbug. When faced with an
armed proletariat, the feuding national
governments immediately united.
The Ultimate Revelation
Class rule is no longer able to disguise itself in
a national uniform; the national governments
are one as against the proletariat!
The Price
Bismarck permitted the slaughter of Paris; in
exchange, Thiers agreed to Bismarck's peace
terms and war indemnities.

The Bloody Week (May 21-28, 1871)
The Massacre
Once the Versailles troops breached the
walls, the massacre of defenseless men,
women, and children reached its zenith.
Over 30,000 citizens of Paris were
slaughtered by mitrailleuse (machine-gun)
fire. 38,000 more were arrested.
The Hypocrisy of Civilization
The civilization and justice of the bourgeois
order stands forth as undisguised savagery
and lawless revenge the moment the
slaves of that order rise against their
masters.

The Vandalism of Defense in Despair
- Incendiarism
The bourgeoisie was convulsed by horror
at the burning of buildings, yet they
shelled Paris for six weeks. The
Commune used fire strictly as a means
of defense to cover their retreat and block
Versailles artillery.

Incendiarism
The bourgeoisie was convulsed by horror at the
burning of buildings, yet they shelled Paris for
six weeks. The Commune used fire strictly as a

Hostages
Thiers routinely executed Communal
prisoners of war. The Commune took
hostages (including the Archbishop)
solely to stop Thiers' firing squads. Thiers
refused all prisoner exchanges, choosing
to sacrifice the Archbishop to justify his
impending carnage.

The True Nature of the International
- The Myth
- The police-tinged bourgeois mind viewed
the International as a secret conspiracy
ordering explosions from a central,
dictatorial body.
The Reality
The International was the organic bond
between the most advanced working men
in the civilized world.
The Conclusion
It cannot be stamped out by carnage. To
stamp it out, governments would have to
stamp out the despotism of capital over
labor-the condition of their own
parasitical existence.

The Ultimate Synthesis
Engels' Postscript (1891):
Of late, the Social-Democratic philistine has once more been filled with
wholesome terror at the words: Dictatorship of the Proletariat. Well and
good, gentlemen, do you want to know what this dictatorship looks like?
Look at the Paris Commune.
That was the Dictatorship of
the Proletariat.
The Insight: The "dictatorship" was not a totalitarian autocracy. It was radically
democratic, decentralized, flat, armed, and managed entirely by the working
class at workmen's wages.

The Legacy
